title: Reliability Explorer
Items Explorer
Documentation
text:
The Peekbank framework has three components:

Processing raw experimental datasets. Each contributed dataset gets a reproducible import script in peekbank-data-import that converts the lab’s raw eye-tracking exports into the standardized peekds format: times re-centered so 0 = target-word onset, gaze resampled to 40 Hz (25 ms samples), looks coded to areas of interest (target / distractor / other / missing). Validators in peekbankr check every table against the schema. Raw inputs and processed outputs are archived in the peekbank_files dataset.
The versioned database. A release build assigns database-wide ids across datasets and publishes the relational tables as a new version of the peekbank dataset on Redivis. Every historical release remains available (see Releases); Peekbank archives all contributed data, including trials and participants the original labs excluded, so users can apply their own criteria.
Interfaces. The peekbankr R package provides high-level accessors; this site’s interactive explorers compute standard analyses in your browser; and the Redivis pages support queries, previews, and exports in any language. See Data Access for all of these.

title: Documentation
text:
Data schema
Peekbank stores every dataset in a common tidy format so cross-dataset analyses are easy. Records are linked by numeric ids (arrows below):

datasets — one row per contributed study: citation info, lab metadata
subjects — one row per (de-identified) child; links longitudinal sessions
administrations — one experimental session: age at test, coding method, tracker and monitor properties
stimuli — word–image pairings, including novelty status
trial_types — the designed trials: target/distractor stimuli and sides, carrier phrase, point of disambiguation, condition
trials — the specific trials a child completed, in order
aoi_region_sets — screen-coordinate definitions of the areas of interest (eye-tracker datasets)
aoi_timepoints — looks coded to target/distractor/other/missing at 40 Hz, time-centered on target-word onset
xy_timepoints — raw gaze coordinates at 40 Hz (eye-tracker datasets)




Peekbank data schema

title: Documentation
text:
Getting started
The fastest route is the Data Access page: install peekbankr, connect, and pull tidy tables in a few lines. For a guided tour of the analyses these data support, open any page in the Analyses menu — every plot has a Data tab with a CSV download of exactly what is shown.

title: Data access
text: Peekbank data live in two versioned, public datasets on Redivis: peekbank (the relational tables) and peekbank_files (raw data, processed intermediates, stimuli, and per-dataset READMEs). Access requires a free Redivis account; the first request from any client opens a browser window to authorize (or set a REDIVIS_API_TOKEN).

title: Data access
text:
R: peekbankr (recommended)
install.packages("redivis", repos = "https://langcog.r-universe.dev", type = "source")
remotes::install_github("peekbank/peekbankr")
library(tidyverse)
library(peekbankr)

con <- connect_to_peekbank()   # pins the current release; prints which one

aoi_timepoints <- get_aoi_timepoints(connection = con, dataset_name = "pomper_saffran_2016")
administrations <- get_administrations(connection = con, dataset_name = "pomper_saffran_2016")

ps_data <- aoi_timepoints %>% left_join(administrations)
Accessors: get_datasets(), get_subjects(), get_administrations(), get_trials(), get_trial_types(), get_stimuli(), get_aoi_region_sets(), get_aoi_timepoints(), get_xy_timepoints(), plus unpack_aux_data() for the JSON aux columns (CDI scores etc.), download_stimuli() and get_readmes() for files, and get_sql_query() for arbitrary SQL. Full reference: peekbank.github.io/peekbankr.

Versions
Peekbank is released in named versions. connect_to_peekbank() uses the latest release by default and announces it; pin any release for reproducibility:
con <- connect_to_peekbank(db_version = "2025.1")
get_db_info()   # lists all available versions
The Redivis-hosted versions correspond to the historical releases 2021.1, 2022.1, 2025.1, 2025.2, and 2026.1 (2021.1 and 2022.1 contain identical data; both are kept for citation stability).

title: Data access
text:
Python and other languages
The redivis-python client reads the same tables:
import redivis

ds = redivis.organization("datapages").dataset("peekbank")
datasets = ds.table("datasets").to_pandas_dataframe()
aoi = ds.query("""
  SELECT * FROM aoi_timepoints_rle
  WHERE administration_id IN (
    SELECT administration_id FROM administrations WHERE dataset_id = 25)
""").to_pandas_dataframe()
Pin versions with dataset("peekbank", version="v1.2"); each version’s release_info table names the Peekbank release it holds. You can also query, explore, and export every table interactively on the Redivis dataset page.

title: Data access
text:
SQL
Redivis datasets are queryable with standard (BigQuery-dialect) SQL — in the browser via each dataset’s Query tab, or through the clients as above. Note for users of the retired MySQL server: string comparison is now case-sensitive, and the aoi_timepoints_indexed helper table no longer exists (aoi_timepoints_rle remains).

title: Data access
text:
Raw data and stimuli
Every dataset’s raw eye-tracking exports, processed peekds CSVs, stimulus images/audio, and README are files in peekbank_files, named by path (<dataset>/raw_data/..., <dataset>/processed_data/..., <dataset>/README.md). Use peekbankr::download_stimuli() / get_readmes(), or browse and download from Redivis directly.

title: Accuracy Explorer
About Peekbank
text:
The Peekbank project aims to make developmental eye-tracking data more accessible for sharing and reuse. We do this by reducing the amount of preprocessing necessary to perform typical analyses and by storing data in a common, tidy format that allows for easy cross-dataset comparisons.
We release new dated versions periodically to facilitate reproducibility (see Releases), and support an API via the peekbankr R package, which lets users access the data in Peekbank without writing queries.
Peekbank is open source and under active development. If you encounter a problem, please file an issue in the GitHub Issues page of the appropriate repository. If you would like to contact us directly, email us at peekbank-dev@lists.stanford.edu.

title: About Peekbank
text:
About this site
The visualizations follow standard analysis conventions for looking-while-listening data (Fernald, Zangl, Portillo, & Marchman, 2008): proportion target looking among target-and-distractor looks; landing-time reaction times on distractor-initial trials; onset-contingent looking curves. Trials excluded by the contributing labs are included by default (Peekbank archives all contributed data), and can be filtered with the “Excluded trials” toggle. Everything is computed in your browser from compact extracts of the current release; the full data live on Redivis.
Built with Quarto and Observable; source at peekbank/peekbank-datapage.

What is peekbank?

html`<p>The <b>peekbank</b> project aims to democratize access to
developmental eye-tracking datasets. The project (1) collects a large set
of eye-tracking datasets using the looking-while-listening paradigm —
currently <b>${totals.datasets} datasets</b> with a total of
<b>${totals.subjects.toLocaleString()} children</b> tested — (2) introduces
a common format and processing tools for such data, and (3) provides
interactive tools and an API for accessing and analyzing the data.</p>`






You can explore the data right in your browser, read the documentation, access the full database via R, Python, or SQL, and browse every dataset. To contribute a dataset, contact peekbank-dev@lists.stanford.edu.
